stories.headline: Padres' Wandy Peralta: Opts in for 2027
stories.detail: Peralta exercised his $4.45 million player option for 2027 on Saturday, Jon Heyman of the New York Post reports. It's the third straight offseason that Peralta has opted in for another year with San Diego. The lefty reliever tossed a career-high 77.1 innings over 65 appearances in the 2026 regular season, posting a 3.61 ERA, 1.32 WHIP and 50:23 K:BB while notching three wins and five holds. Peralta should again be a key part of the Padres ' bullpen in 2027, though that doesn't necessarily mean he'll log frequent high-leverage work.

stories.headline: Nick Pivetta: Becomes free agent
stories.detail: The Padres declined Pivetta 's $14 million option for 2027 on Saturday, Kevin Acee of The San Diego Union-Tribune reports. Pivetta endured an injury-plagued campaign in 2026, as he pitched in only eight regular-season games due to a right flexor strain. The veteran hurler did return for the end of the campaign and looked great in September, recording a 1.45 ERA, 0.91 WHIP and 18:2 K:BB over 18.2 innings across four starts. Pivetta also started two postseason contests, allowing three runs across 7.2 frames while registering an 8:2 K:BB in those outings. Despite the promising finish to the campaign, the Padres opted not to pick up Pivetta's option for 2027, perhaps due in part to the fact that the right-hander would have then had an $18 million player option for 2028. San Diego could still look to re-sign Pivetta on a different deal, though he should draw multiple suitors in free agency given the desirability of reliable starting pitching.

stories.headline: Rays' Yandy Diaz: Option vests for 2027
stories.detail: The Rays have formalized the completion of Diaz 's $13 million vesting option for 2027, Marc Topkin of the Tampa Bay Times reports. Diaz's contract became eligible to vest when Diaz reached 500 plate appearances in August, but he also needed to finish the campaign healthy for the option to kick in. That indeed happened, and the veteran slugger will now be under contract for $13 million next season. Diaz had another strong campaign in 2026, posting a .293/.359/.446 slash line with 22 home runs, 93 runs, 85 RBI and three stolen bases over 154 regular-season games. He batted .333 with two homers in the ALCS to help lead Tampa Bay to the World Series, though he went just 3-for-20 with only one RBI in five games against Milwaukee as the Rays fell short of the title.

stories.headline: Sammy Peralta: Chooses free agency
stories.detail: Peralta elected free agency Saturday. Peralta lost his spot on the 40-man roster when he was outrighted to Triple-A Salt Lake on Thursday. The veteran reliever ultimately decided to turn down that assignment and become a free agent instead. Peralta struggled over 16 appearances between the Rockies and Angels last year, posting a 6.65 ERA, 1.87 WHIP and 23:9 K:BB over 23 innings while notching two holds and one blown save.

stories.headline: Orioles' Colin Selby: Clears waivers, assigned to Triple-A
stories.detail: Selby (shoulder) was reinstated from the 60-day IL, cleared outright waivers, and has been assigned to Triple-A Norfolk. Selby underwent season-ending right shoulder surgery last July to repair his labrum and rotator cuff. He's not expected to be ready for Opening Day in 2027, though there's a good chance he'll be able to return to game action at some point during the summer. Selby didn't pitch at all last year, but he showed some promise in 2025 when he posted a 14:2 K:BB over 14 innings spanning 11 relief appearances with the Orioles while recording a 3.21 ERA and 1.29 WHIP.

stories.headline: Orioles' Codi Heuer: Clears waivers, assigned to Triple-A
stories.detail: Heuer cleared waivers and accepted an outright assignment to Triple-A Norfolk on Saturday. Heuer ended the 2026 campaign in Triple-A before being designated for assignment. Rather than elect free agency, the veteran hurler has chosen to remain in Baltimore's organization. Heuer didn't pitch for the Orioles ' big-league squad last year after being acquired in a trade with Milwaukee in early August. All of his MLB appearances in 2026 came with Cleveland, and he posted a 4.66 ERA, 1.76 WHIP and 6:5 K:BB across 9.2 innings in his eight outings.

stories.headline: Albert Suarez: Elects free agency
stories.detail: Suarez cleared waivers and chose to become a free agent Saturday. Suarez could have accepted an outright assignment to Triple-A Norfolk, but he has instead opted to hit the open market. The 37-year-old pitched in 28 games (all as a reliever) for Baltimore in 2026, posting a 3.86 ERA, 1.22 WHIP and 46:20 K:BB over 63 innings while picking up three wins and one save. Those numbers may be good enough to attract attention from organizations in need of an experienced right-handed pitcher with the ability to cover multiple innings out of the bullpen or even to step in for an occasional spot start.

stories.headline: Rays' Drew Rasmussen: Rays exercise option
stories.detail: The Rays exercised Rasmussen 's $20 million club option for the 2027 season Saturday, Marc Topkin of the Tampa Bay Times reports. Rasmussen made 30 starts in the regular season and spent fewer than 45 days on the injured list in 2026, triggering escalators that elevated the value of his option from $8 million to $20 million. The Rays' decision to bring the 31-year-old back for another season was likely easy despite the price increase, as he posted a 2.67 ERA and 0.91 WHIP across 172 regular-season innings. He also allowed just seven runs in 28.2 frames during the postseason while helping the Rays secure their second American League pennant in seven seasons.

stories.headline: Pierce Johnson: Reds decline mutual option
stories.detail: The Reds declined Johnson 's $8 million mutual option for the 2027 season Saturday. Johnson turned in one of the worst seasons of his career in 2026, finishing the year with a 4.62 ERA and 1.36 WHIP alongside a 42:19 K:BB over 48.2 innings. The Reds will decline to give the right-hander a $2.2 million raise as a result and instead pay him a $1 million buyout to move on. Johnson could still draw some interest in the open market, but he isn't likely to serve as more than a middle reliever in 2027.

stories.headline: Eugenio Suarez: Mutual option declined
stories.detail: The Reds declined Suarez 's $16 million mutual option for 2027 on Saturday. After slugging 49 home runs in 2025, Suarez's production took a step back this season as he slashed .212/.307/.433 with 26 homers, 74 RBI and 50 runs scored across 498 plate appearances. Now a free agent, Suarez still has enough power in his swing that he shouldn't have much trouble finding a team to play for in 2027.
